title: Every point lies in some part of a partition
statement: Let $g : X \times Y \to \alpha$ and let $\mathcal{P}$ be a monochromatic rectangle partition for $g$. Then every point $p \in X \times Y$ belongs to at least one member $R \in \mathcal{P}$.
hypotheses_covered: P is a monochromatic rectangle partition for g
p is an arbitrary point of X × Y
replaced:
If $\mathcal{P}$ is a monochromatic rectangle partition for $g$, then for every
point $p \in X \times Y$ there exists some $R \in \mathcal{P}$ with $p \in R$.
